prompt.context: Your client is Green Dreamz, a vertically-integrated cannabis company based in Colorado, USA. Founded in 2011 as a medical cannabis business, Green Dreamz expanded into the recreational market following state-wide legalization in 2014. Green Dreamz has since become one of the largest players by store count in Colorado, where it competes with companies ranging from mom-and-pop shops to multi-state operators. Green Dreamz operates a cultivation facility in Denver and 12 dispensary locations (3 of which serve medical cannabis only, 4 of which serve recreational cannabis only, and 5 of which serve both). The 12 dispensary locations are spread across the state: 5 in Denver (all of which serve both medical and recreational cannabis), 3 in Colorado Springs (which only allows medical cannabis), 2 in Fort Collins, 1 in Trinidad, and 1 in Cortez. Five of its 12 locations were acquired in 4 separate transactions between 2014 and 2018. As the cannabis industry has matured the market in Colorado has become saturated, and Green Dreamz's organic growth has slowed accordingly. Although Green Dreamz and other companies have invested more in brand-building, consumer preference is still driven primarily by price.
prompt.question: Green Dreamz's CEO has hired your firm to help them find new opportunities for profitable growth. How would you approach this?

clarifying_info.q: What regulations govern the cannabis industry?
clarifying_info.a: Cannabis companies are heavily regulated, with rules governing everything from zoning and operating hours to packaging and advertising. Up to 2 oz of medical cannabis flower (or equivalent in infused products) can be legally sold to registered Colorado patients aged 18+ per day. Up to 1 oz of recreational cannabis flower can be sold to adults aged 21+ per day. Medical infused products can legally have higher potency (100mg+ THC). Federal regulations prohibit cannabis companies from using credit cards; banks are generally unwilling to provide credit or financing. Cannabis products cannot be advertised, shipped, or sold across state lines.

clarifying_info.q: How does Green Dreamz source its products?
clarifying_info.a: Green Dreamz retails all the cannabis flower it grows in-house, and purchases additional flower on wholesale markets to meet demand (especially for recreational dispensaries). Green Dreamz does not produce infused products (edibles, lotions, vape cartridges), but sells those produced by 3rd party manufacturers. Green Dreamz sells 'trim' (parts of the cannabis plant that cannot be sold as flower) to 3rd party manufacturers who extract THC oil for infused products.

clarifying_info.q: What is the breakdown of store types?
clarifying_info.a: 3 medical-only stores, 4 recreational-only stores, and 5 dual medical/recreational stores. Of the 5 dual stores, all are in Denver. Colorado Springs has 3 medical-only stores.

framework: Cannabis Market: Colorado vs. other states; market size and growth trajectory; competitive landscape (market share, mom-and-pop vs. multi-state operators); major trends (supply/demand, consumer preferences, brand building, criminal market, product/packaging innovation, industry consolidation, online ordering/delivery, home-growers); regulatory environment

Green Dreamz Profit Structure: Revenue — B2C (medical vs. recreational differences in prices, customers, avg. spend, visits) and B2B (trim sales); Costs — fixed (rent/utilities, labor, SG&A, R&D, legal) vs. variable (COGS as % of revenue); tax considerations (unusually high federal burden for Schedule I substance)

Growth Opportunities (high level): Organic growth (new cultivation facilities, new dispensaries, infused products division, accessories, branded merchandise, loyalty program); Inorganic growth (acquisitions of dispensaries, cultivation facilities, infused product companies); Out-of-state expansion; Consulting services

questions.prompt: Question 1: What can you infer about the cannabis market in Colorado when looking at Exhibit A?
questions.guidance: Strong answer covers: (1) Fast growth in recreational sales 2014-2017 post-legalization; (2) Growth moderates 2017-2019; (3) Seasonality in recreational sales with annual spikes in July/September; (4) A large spike in 2020, likely pandemic-induced panic buying — candidate should assess whether this is an aberration or indicative of future trends; (5) Medical sales flat 2014-2017, then slight decline 2017-2019 (ceiling on market and/or competition from recreational); slight medical uptick in mid-2020 also pandemic-induced; (6) Wholesale flower prices saw sharp decrease from 2017-2020 coincident with moderating recreational sales growth — potential causes: market saturation, decline in cannabis tourism, oversupply driving price declines, increasing compliance costs, potential resurgence of criminal market.

questions.prompt: Question 2: Calculate the profitability of Green Dreamz using Exhibits B and C along with the store visit data provided.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize they lack price and volume data and ask for it. Present Exhibit B (product mix) and Exhibit C (prices) first; candidate should calculate average medical and recreational spend. Then provide store visit data and costs when asked. Interviewer may encourage candidate to brainstorm cost categories before revealing them. A great candidate calculates pre-tax profit margin (~16%) and comments on whether that is high or low given cannabis companies face unusually high federal tax burdens.

math.setup: Store types: 3 medical-only, 4 recreational-only, 5 dual (90% rec / 10% med). Monthly visits: Medical stores 1,500/store; Recreational stores 9,500/store; Dual stores 5,000/store. Annual costs: Rent/Utilities $10m, Labor $12m, R&D $1m, SG&A $6m, COGS 24% of revenue, Legal $1m. Additional B2B revenue: $2m/year from trim sales.
steps: Trim Revenue = $2,000,000/year (B2B; candidate will likely miss this — interviewer should prompt)
math.answer: Pre-tax profit = $8 million; pre-tax profit margin = 16%. Note: actual after-tax profit will be significantly lower due to unusually high federal tax burden on cannabis companies (Schedule I substance).

questions.prompt: Question 3: What are some ways Green Dreamz can grow its overall revenue?
questions.guidance: Candidate should organize brainstorm into clear buckets (e.g., organic vs. inorganic; near-term vs. long-term; low-risk vs. high-risk). A great candidate structures a 2x2 matrix: existing vs. new customers crossed with existing vs. new products. Cost mitigation should not be the focus. Answers should reflect awareness of cannabis-specific constraints (no interstate sales, limited advertising, cash-only, etc.).

questions.prompt: Question 4: Green Dreamz is considering acquiring Treetops, a smaller competitor. How would you evaluate this opportunity?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure M&A evaluation into buckets: revenue synergies, cost synergies, strategic fit, financial/operational concerns, potential risks, opportunity costs, and valuation. A great candidate builds a mini-framework with 1-2 examples per bucket. Key dimensions: Treetops has an infused products division Green Dreamz lacks; geographic overlap in Denver and Colorado Springs creates cannibalization risk; acquiring medical dispensaries has limited upside given flat/declining medical sales.

questions.prompt: Question 5: What price should Green Dreamz bid for Treetops?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for Treetops financial information to calculate NPV. Should recognize Treetops has a higher profit margin than Green Dreamz (~18% vs 16%) and note this is likely driven by the in-house infused products division. Candidate should ask for discount rate and growth rate. Cannabis companies face higher cost of capital due to bank unwillingness to lend and perceived riskiness. The 6% growth rate is low relative to 58% CAGR in 2013-2016 post-legalization period.

math.setup: Treetops estimated revenue = 30% of Green Dreamz total revenue. Treetops estimated profit margin = 18%. Discount rate = 15% (high due to cannabis industry risk). Growth rate = 6% (low relative to early-legalization era).
math.answer: Bid price should be approximately $30 million (NPV = $30m).

brainstorming.prompt: What are some ways Green Dreamz can grow its overall revenue?

categories.name: Existing customers & existing products
ideas: Price changes or promotions (e.g., happy hours, bundles)

categories.name: Existing customers & new products
ideas: Cannabis cooking classes or educational events

categories.name: New customers & existing products
ideas: Co-op marketing with 3rd party brand partners
Organic expansion to new Colorado geographies (Fort Collins, Grand Junction, Boulder)
Partner with tourism and event companies

categories.name: New customers & new products
ideas: Acquisition of infused product companies, dispensaries, or cultivation facilities
Launch CBD-only products (broader consumer base, fewer regulations)
Consulting services for other cannabis operators

recommendation: Acquire Treetops: The acquisition brings positive revenue synergy opportunities (geographic expansion, new customer access, in-house infused products division for higher margins, cross-sell potential), best practices transfer, and improved value proposition from wider product assortment. At ~$30m NPV it represents a quantifiable entry point.

Do Not Acquire Treetops: Acquiring additional medical dispensaries adds limited value given flat/declining medical sales; cannibalization risk in Denver and Colorado Springs; no current experience operating an infused products division; Green Dreamz would need to purchase even more wholesale flower to supply Treetops dispensaries; potential integration problems given this would be Green Dreamz's largest acquisition. If declining, candidate should propose alternative growth paths from the brainstorm (e.g., in-house infused products organically, CBD launch, loyalty program, geographic expansion).
risks: Acquire: Revenue synergies fail to materialize; increased costs from integration and additional wholesale flower purchases; problems integrating culture and brand; cannibalization in overlapping markets (Denver, Colorado Springs)
Do Not Acquire: Missed opportunity to gain infused products capability and geographic scale; competitor acquires Treetops instead; continued organic growth slowdown without new levers
next_steps: Review Green Dreamz's past acquisition track record and assess integration capabilities before committing
Conduct due diligence on Treetops financials, cultivation facility capacity, and infused products division margins
Model cannibalization impact in Denver and Colorado Springs under combined store count
Assess regulatory feasibility of operating combined entity (licensing, compliance across all locations)
Evaluate alternative organic paths to infused products capability (build vs. buy analysis)
